newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul gets Russian armoured vehicles in debt deal.
newsitem.headline: Seoul gets Russian armoured vehicles in debt deal.

text.p: South Korea's Defence Ministry said on Tuesday that it would take delivery of Russian armoured vehicles this week as part of a debt agreement with Moscow.
"Russian combat vehicles will arrive here in Russian aircraft on Thursday and Saturday," the ministry said in a statement.
The number of tanks to be delivered was not specified.

The ministry also said other Russian defence equipment, including tanks and ammunition, would be shipped to South Korean ports in October under the agreement to pay off long-standing debts with Russian military hardware.
The statement said the BMP-3 armoured vehicles were equipped with guns that could fire conventional and laser-guided shells.
In 1993, South Korea agreed to take $210 million worth of defence equipment as partial repayment of loans which Seoul had extended to the Soviet Union to help its industrial development.
Russia has also agreed to repay the debt in raw materials such as steel and enriched uranium, according to Seoul's Finance and Economy Ministry.
